records.rationale: Retain SpinLockIrq and native irqsave/irqrestore C helpers for configured WrapFD asynchronous I/O completion and result collection. The state is pinned; the closure receives a non-Send guard, exclusively borrows data under the native spinlock and restores the saved flags after any normal return, including a returned error. The closure lifetime prevents escaping the guard or a reference: an extracted-method compile probe accepts an owned value and rejects three escape patterns. The selected caller clones its SharedContext Arc before completion can wake/drop request storage. Send/Sync bounds match protected-data requirements. SDK uses non-RT spinlock semantics; no actual IRQ/concurrency or panic-unwind test is claimed. Existing malformed documentation examples are not treated as compiled doctest evidence.

records.rationale: Retain page_align_down, offset_in_page and is_page_aligned, directly used by WrapFD IoContext bounce-buffer geometry and direct-I/O alignment. These are mask-only operations using the native PAGE_MASK and PAGE_SIZE; they cannot overflow and intentionally describe physical base pages rather than the emulated userspace page size. The caller arithmetic and full I/O algorithm remain separately audited with WrapFD. Native LTS page allocation/mapping operations are not changed by this candidate.

records.rationale: Retain the anon-inode file abstraction used by WrapFD, adapted in f744d35f5a43 to remove &File from the release callback. Native __fput invokes release after the last reference is gone, while File::from_raw_file requires a positive reference count; the ACK wrapper violated this and exposed a refcount-acquirable File during destruction. The new callback receives only owned private data. The selected Wrap implementation uses default destruction, so no consumer source modification is needed; a custom source callback would need to adopt the safer signature. Creation still calls native anon_inode_create_getfile, including !S_PRIVATE inode security initialization and module ownership, returns original private ownership on failure, and transfers exactly one file reference on success. borrow_private requires matching private vtable identity; callbacks keep existing error, compat and VMA conventions. All native fs/anon_inodes.c remains exactly LTS. Extracted creation/release checks pass and the actual ACK control constructs invalid File references. The whole WrapFD driver remains separately reviewed.
